title: Cold & Flu Relief

drivers.name: Price increase (6.2%)
drivers.evidence: Same price in 2026-09-28: sold 13 units (x0.70 vs baseline); 2026-10-05: sold 24 units (x1.30), but baseline was lower; average effect of price hikes on similar products: ~x0.85. Noise-adjusted estimate shrunk to x0.88.

drivers.name: Supplier delivery short
drivers.evidence: Planner note indicates supply risk. No past occurrence at this store, but plausible demand reduction due to stockouts. Downside effect shrunk due to uncertainty.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median of 18.7 is adjusted downward due to a 6.2% price increase (12.03 vs 11.33), which aligns with past price hikes reducing demand. The recent week with the same price (2026-10-05) sold 24 units (x1.30 vs baseline), but the prior week at regular price sold 13 (x0.70), suggesting price sensitivity. The supplier warning of short delivery adds supply risk, lowering expected sales. No events or promotions are scheduled. The classical uplift model suggests no effect, but judgment overrides this due to known price and supply drivers. Evidence is moderate: one past price increase at similar level (2026-09-28), but no prior promotions at this price. The effect is shrunk toward 1.0 due to thin evidence.

brief:
PRODUCT: Cold & Flu Relief | category Health | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-15 (5 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 12.03 (+6.2% vs regular price 11.33)
  planner notes: Supplier warns of a short delivery

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 18.7 | 5%-95%: 3.6 - 38.4 | 10%-90%: 7.5 - 34.0

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-46% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
